abstracts.abstract:
This Act imposes a moratorium, through January 31, 2027, on all applications and permits related to the development of large-scale data centers in this State.

This Act requires a greater than majority vote for passage because § 1 of Article IX of the Delaware Constitution requires the affirmative vote of two-thirds of the members elected to each house of the General Assembly to amend a municipal charter, whether directly, by amendment to a specific municipality’s charter, or as in this Act, indirectly by a general law.

bill.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE LAWS OF DELAWARE RELATING TO A MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTER DEVELOPMENT.

action.description: Defeated By Senate. Votes: 6 YES 15 NO. Reason Taken: Motion to Suspend Rules to Consider SB 353

posted_text:
🏢 DE SB 353 — Delaware Pauses Data Center Plans – Until 2027

A temporary freeze is now in place for new data centers in Delaware.

The law will halt all applications and permit requests for large-scale data centers until January 31, 2027.

This change was made possible by a constitutional requirement needing a two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate to enact this type of general law.

July 27, 2026: Defeated By Senate. Votes: 6 YES 15 NO. Reason Taken: Motion to Suspend Rules to Consider SB 353.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://legis.delaware.gov/BillDetail?LegislationId=143681
